title: Cross-Entropy Loss from Logits
prompt:
Implement `cross_entropy_loss(logits, targets, mask=None)` in PyTorch without calling a ready-made loss.

| Input | Classification | Aligned language-model tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw logits | `(B, C)` | `(B, T, V)` |
| Integer targets | `(B,)` | `(B, T)` |
| Optional boolean mask | `(B,)` | `(B, T)` |

Classes always occupy the **last axis**. Logits are CPU float32 or float64, finite and in `[-10_000, 10_000]`; dimensions are positive. Targets are long tensors. When `mask` is supplied, `True` means include that position; excluded targets may be `-100`. Otherwise every position participates and every target is valid. Included targets are valid class indices. Assume compatible shapes/devices; inputs may be noncontiguous.

For each included position, compute the negative log probability of its target class. Return the **mean over all included positions** as a scalar tensor `()`, preserving logits dtype/device and gradients. Excluded logits must receive zero gradients. Raise `ValueError` if the mask includes no positions. Do not modify inputs.

Use stable tensor primitives such as `log_softmax`, `logsumexp`, and `gather`; do not use `cross_entropy`, `nll_loss`, `CrossEntropyLoss`, or another ready-made loss. The result and gradients must remain finite over the input range. Token logits/targets are **already causally aligned**: do not shift them inside this function. For token inputs, this is a loss mask, not an attention mask: the caller excludes prompt/padding and includes real EOS when appropriate.

Allow about **20–30 minutes**. Follow-ups: Why avoid `log(softmax(logits))`? How does a global token mean differ from averaging each response first? How are SFT, cross-entropy, and KL related?
